To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
calcium is accumulated by smooth muscle cells into elements of the sarcoplasminic reticulum.

1) Calcium is localized in smooth muscle cells in mitochondria and in the elements of sarcoplasmic (sarcotubular) reticulum.2) The sarcoplasmic elements of smooth muscle cells actively accumulate calcium in the presence of oxalate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intracellular localization of Ca2+ in smooth muscle cells and the active accumulation of this cation into the sarcoplasmatic reticulum of smooth muscle cells.
the role of calcium as a regulator of smooth muscle contraction.
the subcellular localization and the active transport of calcium in smooth muscle cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sarcoplasm is the site where calcium is accumulated in smooth muscle.
the calcium-containing structures in smooth muscle are the mitochondria, sarcoplasmic and endoplasmic reticular membranes.
calcium is stored in mitochondria and in sarcoplasmic structures and that the latter are the sites of calcium accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the resting smooth muscle cell calcium is present in the mitochondria and sarcosplasmic reticuli, and that in the activated muscle cell calcium accumulates in the sarcoplasm and is released from the reticuli.
the sarcoplasm of smooth muscle cells is devoid of free calcium ions.
the sarcoplasmatic reticulum is the only calcium-accumulating structure in smooth muscle cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium is a very important part of the contraction process, but it’s not the only thing that’s important.
there is a lot of calcium in smooth muscle cells, but it’s not all in the same place.
the calcium content of mitochondria and sarcoplastic reticulum in smooth muscle cells is low.
